correct_text:
Length (2 octets):
      A 16-bit field indicating the total length, in octets, of the
      subsequent fields.  For this sub-TLV, Length is set to 12.
notes:
Figure 10 (OSPF FADRB Sub-TLV) defines the subsequent value fields following the 4-octet Type (2 octets) and Length (2 octets) header as three 32-bit words totaling 12 octets:

  - Flags: 1 octet
  - Reserved (completing the 32-bit word shown in Figure 10): 3 octets
  - Reference Bandwidth: 4 octets
  - Granularity Bandwidth: 4 octets
  Total = 1 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 12 octets (not 14).

Consistent with OSPF TLV framing rules (RFC 3630 Section 2.3.2, RFC 7684 Section 2.1, RFC 9350 Section 7) and all other OSPF sub-TLVs in RFC 9843 (Section 2.2 Length = 8 = 1 + 3 + 4; Section 3.2.1 Length = 4; Section 3.2.2 Length = 4 = 1 + 3), the Length field specifies the length in octets of the Value portion only and is 12 octets for this sub-TLV.

Setting Length to 14 overstates the payload by 2 octets and violates 4-octet alignment: under RFC 3630 Section 2.3.2 (which pads sub-TLVs to 4-octet boundaries), a standards-compliant receiver rounds Length = 14 up to 16 value octets (20 total octets instead of 16), either rejecting the enclosing OSPF FAD TLV as truncated or skipping 4 octets into the next sub-TLV.

(Secondary note: Figure 10 also omits the explicit field definition for "Reserved (3 octets)" in the "where:" list and shifts the vertical divider between Flags and Reserved slightly left of bit 8 in the ASCII diagram; compare Figure 2 in Section 2.2.)

Length (2 octets):
      A 16-bit field indicating the total length, in octets, of the
      subsequent fields.  For this sub-TLV, Length is set to 4 + N*8
      octets.  Here, N is equal to the number of Threshold Metrics
      specified.  N MUST be greater than or equal to 1.

   Flags (1 octet):
                       0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7
                      +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+
                      |G|             |
                      +-+-+-+-+-+-+-+-+

      G-flag:  When set, Interface Group Mode MUST be used to derive
         total link bandwidth.  Unassigned bits MUST be set to zero and
         MUST be ignored by the receiver.

   Following is the staircase bandwidth threshold and associated metric
   values.

   Bandwidth Threshold 1 (4 octets):
      Minimum Link Bandwidth is encoded in IEEE floating point format
      (32 bits)[IEEE754-2019].  The units are bytes per second.

   Threshold Metric 1 (4 octets):
      Metric value range (1 - 4,294,967,295 (0xFFFFFFFF))

   Bandwidth Threshold N (4 octets):
      Maximum Link Bandwidth is encoded in IEEE floating point format
      (32 bits)[IEEE754-2019].  The units are bytes per second.

   Threshold Metric N (4 octets):
      Metric value range (1 - 4,294,967,295 (0xFFFFFFFF))

   When the G-flag is set, the cumulative bandwidth of the parallel
   links is computed as described in Section 4.1.1.2.  If the G-flag is
   not set, the advertised Maximum Link Bandwidth is used.

   The assignment of the Bandwidth Metric based on computed link
   bandwidth is described below.

   During the Flex-Algorithm SPF calculation, the Bandwidth Metric for a
   link MUST be assigned according to the following rules:

   1.  When the computed link bandwidth is less than Bandwidth Threshold
       1:

       The Bandwidth Metric MUST be set to the maximum metric value of
       4,294,967,295.
notes:
Section 4.1.4.2 (OSPF FADBT Sub-TLV, Figure 11) contains two normative arithmetic errors that cause wire-framing and 32-bit integer overflow failures:

1. Sub-TLV Length formula ("2 + N*8" -> "4 + N*8"):
   Following the 4-octet Type (2 octets) and Length (2 octets) header, Figure 11 contains a 32-bit word consisting of Flags (1 octet) and Reserved (3 octets) — totaling 4 octets, not 2 octets — followed by N pairs of Bandwidth Threshold (4 octets) and Threshold Metric (4 octets), totaling N*8 octets. The total length of subsequent fields is therefore 4 + N*8 octets (e.g., 12 octets for N = 1, 20 octets for N = 2).
   Setting Length to 2 + N*8 understates the payload by 2 octets for every N >= 1 (e.g., Length = 10 for N = 1), truncating the last 2 octets of Threshold Metric N and breaking 4-octet OSPF sub-TLV alignment (RFC 3630 Section 2.3.2, RFC 9350 Section 7).

2. Maximum 32-bit OSPF metric value ("4,294,967,296" -> "4,294,967,295"):
   0xFFFFFFFF equals 2^32 - 1 = 4,294,967,295, whereas 4,294,967,296 equals 2^32 = 0x100000000, which requires 33 bits and cannot be represented in a 4-octet (32-bit) unsigned integer (wrapping to 0 on uint32 assignment). Both the Threshold Metric range descriptions ("1 - 4,294,967,296 (0xFFFFFFFF)") and normative Rule 1 ("MUST be set to the maximum metric value of 4,294,967,296") contradict RFC 9843 Section 2.2 ("4,294,967,295 (0xFFFFFFFF)"), Section 4.1.4.1 ("0xFFFFFFFF"), and RFC 9350 Section 15.3 ("(2^32 - 1) in OSPF").
